newsitem.title: UK: Britain to clamp road tax dodgers.
newsitem.headline: Britain to clamp road tax dodgers.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday that it would launch a national scheme to wheelclamp and impound vehicles for which vehicle excise duty has not been paid early in 1997.

"Car tax dodgers are costing the taxpayer around 170 million pounds a year and are a source of resentment for the law-abiding motorists," Transport Secrtary Sir George Young said in a statement issued with the UK budget statement.
Describing the move as a "tough measure", Young said contractors would be asked to put forward proposals for introducing the scheme as quickly as possible.
Offending drivers will have to pay a release fee of 68 pounds and tax their vehicle. Evaders would also face prosecution with a maximum fine of 1,000 pounds.
UK Chancellor Kenneth Clarke announced a five pounds rise in car vehicle excise duty to 145 pounds in his budget statement earlier on Tuesday.
